### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/plugin-audit`, touching **5** documentable anchor(s).

**11** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/data-modeling/drivers.mdx`  _(via OS_DATABASE_URL (literal, a string literal in flags))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/external-datasources.mdx`  _(via OS_DATABASE_URL (literal, a string literal in flags))_
- `content/docs/deployment/backup-restore.mdx`  _(via OS_DATABASE_URL (literal, a string literal in flags))_
- `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx`  _(via OS_DATABASE_URL (literal, a string literal in flags), database_busy (literal, a string literal in rewrite), os migrate audit-side-copies (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/audit-side-copies.ts))_
- `content/docs/deployment/environment-variables.mdx`  _(via OS_DATABASE_URL (literal, a string literal in flags))_
- `content/docs/deployment/production-readiness.mdx`  _(via OS_DATABASE_URL (literal, a string literal in flags))_
- `content/docs/deployment/self-hosting.mdx`  _(via OS_DATABASE_URL (literal, a string literal in flags))_
- `content/docs/deployment/single-project-mode.mdx`  _(via OS_DATABASE_URL (literal, a string literal in flags))_
- `content/docs/getting-started/your-first-project.mdx`  _(via OS_DATABASE_URL (literal, a string literal in flags))_
- `content/docs/plugins/index.mdx`  _(via OS_DATABASE_URL (literal, a string literal in flags))_
- `content/docs/upgrading.mdx`  _(via os migrate audit-side-copies (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/audit-side-copies.ts))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **5** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **45** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c32bb6ccbb293a4bda77010ce7ad416fcfeb1138` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `8821ca81af391c7f57cb07055caef997cba14f5e` — the merge of head `34582583df4b86a5250a4adefee4d4f7a3ae3521` into base `c32bb6ccbb293a4bda77010ce7ad416fcfeb1138`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 8821ca81af391c7f57cb07055caef997cba14f5e && git checkout 8821ca81af391c7f57cb07055caef997cba14f5e
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin c32bb6ccbb293a4bda77010ce7ad416fcfeb1138 34582583df4b86a5250a4adefee4d4f7a3ae3521 && git checkout -B drift-repro c32bb6ccbb293a4bda77010ce7ad416fcfeb1138 && git merge --no-ff 34582583df4b86a5250a4adefee4d4f7a3ae3521

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c32bb6ccbb293a4bda77010ce7ad416fcfeb1138
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs c32bb6ccbb293a4bda77010ce7ad416fcfeb1138` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `34582583df4b86a5250a4adefee4d4f7a3ae3521`
Local-runs: none

Read: the PR's two commits on top of `main`, `0c23193a` (pins, docs, changeset) and `34582583` (code). That is 12 files, +861/−11. I diffed the new command line by line against its twin `audit-key-material.ts` and checked each claim against the code at this head. CI was still running when I read it: 31 success, 23 skipped, 7 in progress, 1 cancelled, 0 failed.

### ① Derived judgments

**The driver is the twin, plus `--object`.** A `diff` against `packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/audit-key-material.ts` shows only names, wording, the `--object` block and the `objects` field it threads through. Each point the area asked about:

- *Dry run writes nothing.* A dry run boots read-only with `deferSchemaDdl` and `readOnlyProbe` (`audit-side-copies.ts:220`, twin `:191`), and both runners get `apply: false` (`:256`, `:265`). Pin 1 compares both SQLite files row for row before and after the dry run (`audit-side-copies.archive.integration.test.ts:301-302`).
- *`--apply` needs confirmation.* `--apply` without `--yes` exits 1 under `--json` or when stdin is not a TTY, and prompts on a TTY (`:180-198`, twin `:151`). The command joins the `migrate-confirmation-exit.pin.test.ts` roster (`:257`).
- *Refusals are counted.* `refused` adds the hot report and every archive report (`:268`). Either a refusal or a failure exits 1 on both output paths (`:273`, `:341`, twin `:247`, `:315`). The human report prints `N sealed and refused` per table and per store (`:283`, `:291`).
- *Archive classification.* It uses the shared `examineArchiveTargets` and `archiveFailureCount` from `utils/ledger-copy-archive.ts`, with the same four `status` branches and messages (`:260-266`, `:294-324`). The only change is `tables: objects` instead of the fixed list, so `--object sys_activity` gives `archive: []`. Pin 2 measures that (`test:319`).
- *Exit codes.* They match the twin on every path: busy without `--force`, confirmation required, boot error, a failure, a refusal, and an archive that is `not-connected` or `unknown`. The one new path, an unknown `--object`, exits 1.
- *`--json` stdout stays pure.* The runner logger goes to stderr under `--json` (`:238-239`), and every error path uses `emitJson`. The refusal path runs before `reserveStdoutForJson`, but it prints nothing except the one `emitJson` document, and pin 6 parses its whole stdout as JSON (`test:370`). The command joins `json-stdout-purity.e2e.test.ts` (`:136-138`).
- *`--object` is checked before the boot.* The check runs at `:136-151`, before `probeMigrationTarget` (`:155`), the confirmation (`:180`), `composeRedactionSeal` (`:205`) and `bootSchemaStack` (`:212`). The only thing it loads first is `@objectstack/plugin-audit`, for `SIDE_COPY_TABLES`. Duplicate names are dropped, and the table order comes from `SIDE_COPY_TABLES`, not from the flag order.

**Audit data stays safe.**
- The seal is wired as in the twin. `composeRedactionSeal()` runs before the boot (`:205`), its plugins join the boot (`:215`), and the same `seal` object goes to the hot run (`:256`) and to every archive run (`:265`). The command joins `audit-redaction-seal.contract.test.ts` (`:25`).
- The rewrite goes through the shared `runLedgerCopyRewrite` (`side-copy-migration.ts:161-182`). That is the code path that amends a sealed row before rewriting it, or refuses the row. So a sealed or chained row is never rewritten without its amendment.
- The live suite (`audit-seal-redaction-live.integration.test.ts`) now amends a sealed `sys_approval_request` copy through `migrateSideCopies`. It asserts that the copy loses `payload_json`, that the amendment's `rewritten_by` is `os migrate audit-side-copies`, and that the verifier reads the row as `redacted`.

**The `rewritten_by` rename.**
- The value is free text. The amendment writer signs it into the body (`amendment-writer.ts:414`), and the verifier reads it back as text (`signed-body.ts:338`). Nothing checks it against a list of names, so an amendment signed earlier under `side-copy-migration` still verifies.
- The old value never shipped. `side-copy-migration.ts` does not exist at tag `@objectstack/plugin-audit@18.4.0`, the newest release (published 2026-11-13T12:33Z): the contents API answers 404 at that ref. #33117 (`3eac63a9`, 2026-11-13T21:02Z) added it after that release, and its changeset `.changeset/mcp-read-tools-ai-readable-system-object.md` is still pending.

**The pins measure the claims,** with one gap, N1. Cases 0–5 drive the real Archiver and the source CLI. They compare both stores row for row, check which keys survive in a rewritten copy (`test:347-349`), check that the same-named column on an unlisted object is kept (`:341-342`), and check that a re-run changes nothing (`:357`). `data-commands.absent-database.integration.test.ts` adds a live `sys_activity` copy, so the hot activity path rewrites a row (`rewritten: 1`). Pin 2's `sys_activity` has no rows in this fixture. What it shows is the exclusion: `sys_audit_log` is left alone in both stores.

**The docs match the behaviour.** In `cli.mdx`, the section's flags, the `OBJECT_NOT_FOUND` refusal, the per-table and per-store report and the archive cross-reference match the code. The sealed-rows paragraph and the absent-database paragraph now list the new command. The `upgrading.mdx` line says "from 18.4.0 or earlier", which is right, because the writer change it cleans up after is not released yet.

### ② Semver level

- *`Clause-②: yes (widening)` is right.* The PR adds a CLI command, the `--object` flag and an `objects` member in the `--json` document. Nothing that was accepted before is refused now. `--object` is new, so refusing an unknown value narrows nothing.
- *The `rewritten_by` change is not a narrowing.* It is a stored value, and only new amendments carry it. No reader matches on it. No release ever wrote `side-copy-migration`, so no deployment holds an amendment that a reader could misread. A row amended on a pre-release build keeps its signed value and still verifies. The changeset says this.
- *Patch for both packages is right.* No authorable metadata or spec shape moves, so `Metadata-protocol: none` holds. Both declaration lines start a line in the PR body and in `.changeset/33155-audit-side-copies-door.md`. No `!`, BREAKING banner or ADR-0087 marker is owed.

### ③ Boundary flags

None. The diff stays in `packages/cli`, the plugin-audit migration's name and comment, two docs pages and the family rosters. It builds no lock; ADR-0154 P4b3 is left to its own slice, as the PR says.

**Nits (none blocks).**
- N1. Pin 6 is titled "refused before anything is read" (`audit-side-copies.archive.integration.test.ts:367`), but it measures only exit 1, `OBJECT_NOT_FOUND` and an unchanged hot store. A refusal after the boot would pass it too. To pin "before the boot", point that run's `--database-url` at a file that does not exist and assert the file is still absent afterwards. Run with `--apply --yes`, the plain boot would create it.
- N2. The `cli.mdx:1485` table row now names `--object` and then says "No flag; idempotent". The siblings use "No flag" to mean no `sys_migration` flag is recorded, but next to a CLI flag it reads as a contradiction. "Records no `sys_migration` flag" would be exact.
- N3. Three code-comment rosters of the family were not updated: `utils/ledger-copy-archive.ts:7` names two commands, `audit-seal/amendment-writer.ts:24-26` names three, and `utils/schema-migrate.ts:1276-1279` says `composeDeclaredDatasources` is set "by nothing else". That last one was already stale, because `os audit verify` sets it too.
- N4. The `--object` refusal at `audit-side-copies.ts:137-142` repeats `refuseUndeclaredObjects` (`utils/migrate-object-scope.ts:73-91`) with a different message. Calling the helper with `SIDE_COPY_TABLES` as the declared set would keep one envelope builder. The helper's message says "this deployment declares", so it would need a small message option.

Implemented-by: `claude/area-A2-33155`
Reviewed-by: `session_016WV4d1PGptBW3QRQNmy5e6`

**VERDICT: PASS**

The `rewritten_by` rename is not a narrowing: the old value shipped in no release, and the verifier reads the value as free signed text. The four nits, N1 to N4, are not blocking and are left for a follow-up touch.
- CI at this head: 39 success and 17 expected skips, nothing unexpected. One `Check Changeset` run was cancelled because a newer run of the same check superseded it; both of the other runs succeeded.
- Governed-surface predicate: not governed. 872 changed lines (≤ 3000).
- Base: mergeable state is clean, and the head is 12 commits behind `main`. The PR touches `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/plugin-audit` and docs, and none of these is a shared package under the before-arming rule.
- Scope: closes #33155 (`os migrate audit-side-copies`).

Landing: ready for review, then auto-merge (the area rule for PRs that passed review, 2026-11-15T03:10Z).
